ai.description: Bhupathy’s Bent-toed Gecko reaches 75 mm snout-vent length. It is brownish with dark dorsal bands and possesses slender, curved digits and a distinct, granular dorsal scalation.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus bhupathyi* is distinguished by the presence of 18–20 longitudinal rows of enlarged, strongly keeled dorsal tubercles, which are more numerous than in most congeners.
ai.habitat: Cyrtodactylus bhupathyi inhabits moist deciduous forests in the Western Ghats, specifically dwelling on rocky outcrops and boulders at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: Bhupathy’s bent-toed gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among rocky outcrops and vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus bhupathyi* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus bhupathyi* is endemic to the Western Ghats in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu, specifically inhabiting high-elevation rocky outcrops in the Anaimalai Hills.
